key_insight: Machine-learning models, especially DCN, can accurately predict buckling resistance of welding-strengthened circular steel tubes and help turn complex thermo-mechanical effects into a practical design formula.
engineering_relevance: The study offers a deployable resistance prediction approach for strengthening CHS members, improving design reliability when welding-induced distortion and residual stress would otherwise be difficult to account for.
method: Built 800 FE samples from 400 configurations using sequentially coupled thermo-mechanical simulation of loading, welding, cooling, and re-loading.
Trained KNN, AdaBoost, ANN, and DCN models to predict stability factor, deflection amplification, and post-strengthening compressive stress.
Used SHAP to identify the dominant drivers and assembled an explicit buckling-resistance formula with service-load reduction and column-curve selection.
evidence_signal: DCN achieved test-set R² values above 0.992 for all three targets, and the final formula reached a mean predicted-to-FE resistance ratio of 0.952 with 6.03% MAPE.
watch_item: The formula is calibrated on simulated FE data for a specific strengthened CHS setup, so transferability to other geometries, weld details, or material grades should be validated before use.
paper_title: Machine learning-based prediction formulas for buckling resistance of welding-strengthened circular steel tubes
